annotations.description: With only 1 mana available (Blood Crypt), the player chose Seal of Fire over Nethergoyf. Nethergoyf as a 1/2 (creature type in graveyard from Street Wraith) provides a body that can block and apply pressure, while Seal of Fire is merely a 2-damage removal spell sitting on the battlefield. However, Seal of Fire does add an enchantment type to the graveyard when sacrificed, which would grow Nethergoyf later. The key consideration is that Nethergoyf could have been cast now as a 1/2 and would grow as more card types enter the graveyard, while Seal of Fire doesn't impact the board meaningfully on its own. That said, Seal of Fire provides flexible removal and adds a card type to graveyard (enchantment) when used, so this is debatable rather than clearly wrong.

annotations.description: Discarding Goryo's Vengeance when there's no legendary creature in the graveyard to target, but the card has future potential. The player has Solitude in hand which could be evoked (putting it in the graveyard) and then targeted with Goryo's Vengeance for a powerful tempo play with Ephemerate to make it permanent. Discarding one copy is acceptable since they have two, but Winternight Stories or one of the Ephemerates might be better discard candidates. Winternight Stories is a 3-mana sorcery that draws 3 and discards (decent but slow), while the Goryo's + Ephemerate + Solitude combo is the deck's primary game plan. Having two Goryo's Vengeance provides redundancy for this critical combo piece.

annotations.description: Casting Thoughtseize before playing Undercity Sewers is slightly suboptimal sequencing. Undercity Sewers enters tapped so it won't help cast anything this turn, but playing it first would trigger surveil 1, putting a card into the graveyard which could add a third card type (land) to the graveyard for Nethergoyf (currently 2 types: sorcery and creature). More importantly, the land drop costs no mana and should generally be done before spending mana on spells. Additionally, Thoughtseize costs 2 life (going to 16), and the life loss matters for Death's Shadow. The sequencing error is minor since the Undercity Sewers enters tapped anyway and doesn't change available mana this turn, but the surveil information could have informed the Thoughtseize decision.

annotations.description: Taking Goryo's Vengeance over Solitude is debatable. Solitude is the opponent's best removal spell and can be evoked for free to exile key threats like Death's Shadow or Moonshadow. Goryo's Vengeance currently has no legendary creatures in the opponent's graveyard to reanimate (only Polluted Delta and the Goryo's Vengeance itself are there), making it a lower immediate threat. Solitude, on the other hand, is always live as premium removal that can blow out the Sonnet Critic's game plan. However, Goryo's Vengeance could become very dangerous if a Quantum Riddler or Solitude ends up in the graveyard later, and denying a reanimation combo piece has merit. The opponent also has Ephemerate x2 which combos powerfully with Solitude (evoke Solitude, then Ephemerate it to keep it and get another exile trigger), but taking Solitude would break up that combo more directly.
